a: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by (ā before consonants)
ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by

accipiunt: accipiō, accipere, accēpī, acceptum — to take in, receive (3rd pl. pres.)

ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
agmina: agmen, agminis (n.) — marching column, host, troop (acc./nom. pl.)

alta: altus, -a, -um — high; deep (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
ante: ante (prep. + acc., adv.) — before, in front of; previously

certo: certus, -a, -um — fixed, sure, certain (n./m. abl./dat. sg.)

dedere: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, give forth (3rd pl. perf. = dedērunt)
defessi: dēfessus, -a, -um — worn out, exhausted (m. nom. pl.)

fit: fīō, fierī, factus sum — to be made, become, come about (3rd sg. pres.)

hectore: Hector, Hectoris (m.) — Hector, Trojan champion, son of Priam (abl. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
hominumque: homō, hominis (m.) — human being, man (gen. pl.) + -que 'and'
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
ibat: eō, īre, iī (īvī), itum — to go (3rd sg. impf.)

illo: ille, illa, illud — that (m./n. abl. sg.)
illos: ille, illa, illud — that; he, they (m. acc. pl.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
incipit: incipiō, -ere, incēpī, inceptum — to begin, start (3rd sg. pres.)

magna: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, mighty (f. abl./nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
mihi: ego, meī — I; mihi, to/for me (dat.)
mille: mille (indecl.) — a thousand; pl. mīlia, -ium (n.), thousands

moenia: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (nom./acc. pl.)
morsu: morsus, -ūs (m.) — bite, grip, fluke (of an anchor) (abl. sg.)
mortalibus: mortālis, -e — mortal; mortālēs (m. pl.), men (dat. pl.)

nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor

nos: ego, meī — I; nōs, we, us (nom./acc. pl.)
numina: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, god (nom./acc. pl.)

omnis: omnis, -e — all, every (acc. pl., = omnēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
operi: opus, operis (n.) — work, task, labour (dat. sg.)
ora: ōs, ōris (n.) — mouth, face; pl. faces, features (acc./nom. pl.)
pars: pars, partis (f.) — part, share, portion (nom. sg.)
patria: patria, -ae (f.) — fatherland, native country, land (nom./abl. sg.)
patrios: patrius, -a, -um — of one's father, native, ancestral (m. acc. pl.)
pedes: pēs, pedis (m.) — foot (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)

perque: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, over, by + -que 'and'
petunt: petō, -ere, petīvī, petītum — to seek, aim at, ask (3rd pl. pres.)
plurima: plūrimus, -a, -um — most, very many (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
post: post (adv.; prep. + acc.) — afterwards, hereafter; after, behind

quales: quālis, -e — of what sort, what kind of (interrog., m. nom. pl.)
qualis: quālis, -e — of what sort; such as, like, as (m./f. nom. sg.)

quorum: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., m./n. gen. pl.)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)

sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)

sedes: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc./nom. pl.)
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sorte: sors, sortis (f.) — lot; allotment, portion, fate (abl. sg.)
spes: spēs, speī (f.) — hope, expectation (nom. sg.; also acc. pl.)

subit: subeō, subīre, subiī, subitum — to go under, approach, enter (3rd sg. pres.)
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)

tantae: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. gen./dat. sg.; f. nom. pl.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)

tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuorum: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.); tuōrum, of your people (m. gen. pl.)

ulixes: Ulixēs, -is (m.) — Ulysses, king of Ithaca (nom. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides

ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
varios: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (m. acc. pl.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or

virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
